item.title: Strategy Cannot Survive a Polluted Culture
item.description:
“Show me the incentive and I’ll show you the outcome.” — Charlie Munger

In the “who eats whom” debate between Strategy, Execution, or Culture, I would argue that Strategy “eats” Execution and Culture is the water in which everyone swims. Strategy is not a by-product of culture, but it does determine which strategies can survive within an organization. Rather than putting a premium on strategy, where A.I. has become a mandate, it has polluted waters in which strategic thinking previously flourished.

item.title: Why Marketers Will Get A.I. Wrong Before They Get It Right
item.description: A.I. won't fix marketing's measurement problems — but it will expose them. The real challenge isn't learning to prompt; it's learning to think.

item.title: About
item.description:
This website is an experiment.

I built it using Hugo and GitHub Pages, learning the technical stack from scratch with A.I. assistance — not because I needed a website, but because I wanted to understand how large language models consume, interpret, and prioritize content. That curiosity started with an AEO/GEO roadmap I was developing for my brands and has since expanded into a broader question: what does it actually mean to work effectively with A.I. in a marketing context?
